description:
Reorganize the cohesive Channel delivery subsystem under Zaq.Channels.Delivery with behavior unchanged. User approved the namespace/folder direction and requested this execution issue. Work in the existing feat/channel-files working tree, preserving all uncommitted implementation from zaq-1lw.20.

Module/file mapping:
- Zaq.Channels.DeliveryAttachments -> Zaq.Channels.Delivery.Attachments; lib/zaq/channels/delivery/attachments.ex
- Zaq.Channels.DeliveryPlan -> Zaq.Channels.Delivery.Plan; lib/zaq/channels/delivery/plan.ex
- Zaq.Channels.DeliveryPlan.Step -> Zaq.Channels.Delivery.Plan.Step; lib/zaq/channels/delivery/plan/step.ex
- Zaq.Channels.DeliveryExecutor -> Zaq.Channels.Delivery.Executor; lib/zaq/channels/delivery/executor.ex
- Zaq.Channels.DeliveryConfirmation -> Zaq.Channels.Delivery.Confirmation; lib/zaq/channels/delivery/confirmation.ex
- Zaq.Channels.DeliveryError -> Zaq.Channels.Delivery.Error; lib/zaq/channels/delivery/error.ex

Keep Zaq.Channels.TransportRequirements at lib/zaq/channels/transport_requirements.ex: it is the shared bridge transport contract. Keep Zaq.Engine.Messages.Outgoing.Delivery under Engine: it owns shared outgoing data, not Channel orchestration. Avoid ambiguous Delivery aliases where both appear; use explicit module paths or descriptive local aliases. Existing provider-local Zaq.Channels.JidoChatBridge.DeliveryResult and Zaq.Channels.Web.Delivery remain with their respective owners. Do not move modules merely because their names contain delivery.

Scope:
1. Inspect live Git/Beadwork state, module responsibilities and references before editing. Reuse the implemented findings 1–8; do not reset/revert/reimplement zaq-1lw.20.
2. Move and rename the six modules atomically with their aliases, struct literals, nested Step references, specs, behaviours/callback type references, imports, configured module references, and any runtime module references.
3. Audit cross-service consumers, notably Outgoing.Delivery.plan's type, Agent/Engine consumers, Channels Api, Bridge, JidoChatBridge, EmailBridge, notification/history paths, and test support. Investigate serialized module identities only if actual persistence exists; these plans/prepared values are supposed to be transient. Do not add speculative compatibility shims.
4. Move the owning suites into test/zaq/channels/delivery/attachments_test.exs, executor_test.exs, confirmation_test.exs, error_test.exs, and update their module names. Move any independently owned Plan/Step suite discovered during the audit consistently. Update references in other suites without changing assertions or scenarios.
5. Update active repository documentation/module docs and paths. Do not rewrite historical records or externally publish/edit the background Page without authorization.
6. Remove superseded source paths. Do not introduce a Delivery facade or new public functions just to populate the namespace.

Acceptance:
- New namespace compiles, all live consumers use it, and old host module names remain only in intentionally preserved historical material.
- Outgoing.delivery still uses Engine's typed Delivery and plan remains transient/private.
- Metadata-only planning, execution-time materialization, selected-connector failure policy, stop barriers, continue behavior, existing thread ownership, confirmation/history semantics, errors and return shapes are unchanged.
- No work on candidates 9–14, Telegram dependency expansion, scheduling redesign, new APIs, new Actions/tools or configuration changes.

Action reuse assessment: local-only namespace/data-contract reorganization. Reuse existing functions and operations unchanged; no new executable operation or wrapper is justified. Read docs/action-reuse.md and verify this assessment against the actual diff.

Policies: AGENTS.md; docs/agent-tools.md; docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md; docs/conventions.md; docs/code-quality.md; docs/documentation.md; docs/testing-approach.md; applicable Channels/Engine/Agent service guides before affected work. Use module-context/safe-refactor/code-quality skills as applicable. Existing-test behavioral changes are not part of this issue; obtain approval if an unexpected contract change becomes necessary.

Validation: run mix q and isolated moved suites plus affected planner/policy/API/Jido/email/Agent/Engine confirmation journeys. Search for stale module references, inspect the final diff and run git diff --check. Verify compiled structs and Inspect implementations use the new names; avoid relying on stale BEAM modules. No redundant implementation-mirroring tests for renames. Preserve meaningful existing assertions. Respect existing review/coverage/E2E/final-precommit lifecycle; do not close pending approval gates.

Known baseline: previous focused review passed 503/504 checks. The retained Telegram exact-byte delivery failure is tracked by zaq-1lw.21 (installed adapter lacks file_requirements/1); do not weaken it or silently absorb its fix. Broader browser/finalization blockers are recorded under the parent epic. Recheck current state rather than assuming the baseline is unchanged.

Report module mappings, consumers audited, validations, baseline versus new failures, and remaining gates. No commit/push/publication unless separately authorized.

comments.text:
Pre-edit audit: feat/channel-files is clean at b176f8ca7, so all zaq-1lw.20 work is already preserved in HEAD; no uncommitted changes to overwrite. Current full-suite evidence on this same commit is 12249/12250 PASS, 366/366 properties, sole Telegram SDK requirements failure zaq-1lw.21. Parent eight-finding decisions supersede original epic prose. No Telegram expansion or candidates 9–14.

Module-context assessment: Attachments owns metadata grouping/materialization preparation; Plan and Plan.Step own transient metadata descriptions; Executor owns tasks, acquired/prepared bytes, outcomes and elected roots; Confirmation owns receipt projection and Engine reporting; Error owns bounded failure facts/private diagnostics. Flow remains Api or direct bridge -> Attachments -> Executor -> provider operation -> Confirmation -> existing Engine event/history. Inputs, policy/defaults, authorization, dependencies, ordering, timeouts, effects, error shapes, Inspect exclusions and lifetime remain unchanged.

Concrete consumers: Channels Api, Bridge callback specs, JidoChatBridge, EmailBridge, SmtpSender module documentation, CommunicationBridge documentation and TransportRequirements.Error references; Engine.Messages.Outgoing.Delivery.plan type; BO NotificationSmtpLive error pattern; TestSupport.DeliveryDiagnostics traced MFA. Agent producers remain unchanged; AttachmentSelectionDeliveryTest consumes Attachments. Engine history/confirmation, Outgoing constructors, email and Jido/API/policy/journey suites reference the six modules and must migrate. Existing tests and source confirm Confirmation clears private plans before Engine recording and Outgoing.Delivery.from_result discards producer plans; no persisted plan/module identity found. Engine history/Web delivery and provider-local JidoChatBridge.DeliveryResult retain ownership and names. No direct Delivery alias will be introduced; Outgoing.Delivery remains explicit.

Safe-refactor plan: move six source files plus four owning suites; migrate declarations/aliases/structs/specs/callbacks/MFAs and active guide links atomically. No standalone Plan/Step suite exists. Use Attachments/Plan/Executor/Confirmation/Error aliases from Zaq.Channels.Delivery while preserving unrelated aliases. Update Channels and message-lifecycle guides; preserve historical handoff records. Existing module implementations/functions remain identical apart from module identifiers and diagnostic module label. No new functions, facade, wrappers, fixtures, behavior expectations or dependencies.

Action reuse assessment: local-only namespace/data-contract reorganization; reuse all existing delivery operations unchanged, including Materialization/DecodeBase64, provider operations and NodeRouter receipt recording. No Action/tool addition or duplicate operation justified. Verification: moved suites plus policy/API/Jido/email/Agent/Engine journeys; fresh project compilation with stale-module/Inspect checks, mix q, normalized implementation/assertion equivalence, stale-reference search and diff check. Rollback criterion: reject any semantic change or need to weaken tests; fix only migration errors. E2E unnecessary for pure refactor, existing feature UX/review/coverage/precommit gates remain open. No commit/push/publication authorized.
